definitions.explanation: An employee who is hired by a staffing agency and dispatched to work at a client company. A common form of non-regular employment in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}いている→働く：00503_hataraku⟧。
examples.english: She is working as a temporary worker.

examples.japanese: {派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{契約|けいやく}→契約：02698_keiyaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来月|らいげつ}→来月：00744_raigetsu⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{切|き}れる→切れる：01936_kireru⟧。
examples.english: The temp worker's contract expires next month.

examples.japanese: {派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{正社員|せいしゃいん}→正社員：13194_seishain⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{登用|とうよう}→登用：17153_touyou⟧⟦される→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{会社|かいしゃ}→会社：00607_kaisha⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: More companies are introducing systems to promote temporary workers to full-time employees.

notes:
USAGE:
A key term in understanding Japanese employment. Dispatch workers are employed by a ⟦{派遣|はけん}→派遣：13273_haken⟧{会社|がいしゃ} (staffing agency) but work at a different company. They typically have less job security and fewer benefits than ⟦{正社員|せいしゃいん}→正社員：13194_seishain⟧ (regular employees).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{働|はたら}く→働く：00503_hataraku⟧ (to work as a temp)
- {派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{契約|けいやく}→契約：02698_keiyaku⟧ (temp worker's contract)
- {派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{雇|やと}う→雇う：02320_yatou⟧ (to hire dispatch workers)
- {派遣|はけん}{社員|しゃいん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{正社員|せいしゃいん}→正社員：13194_seishain⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧ (from temp to regular employee)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{正社員|せいしゃいん}→正社員：13194_seishain⟧: regular/full-time employee — permanent position with full benefits
- ⟦{契約|けいやく}{社員|しゃいん}→契約社員：12260_keiyakushain⟧: contract employee — hired directly by the company on a fixed-term contract
- ⟦パート→パート：03106_paato⟧: part-time worker — typically shorter hours, common for homemakers
